content_units: You have a realistic path into instructional design within   12 months  , especially with   8 years of teaching  , curriculum design experience, and presentation skills already in place. Your strongest entry angle is   learning design / instructional designer roles in corporate L&D, higher education, training providers, and public-sector learning teams   in Dublin.
Best-fit target:   junior-to-mid instructional designer, learning designer, eLearning developer, or L&D content specialist   roles aiming for   €48,000+  , with the strongest odds if you build:
- corporate-style language on your CV and LinkedIn

Months 1-2   Reframe your profile   Translate teaching into L&D language; learn ADDIE, adult learning, Bloom’s, Kirkpatrick basics; refresh Canva and slide design   Updated CV, LinkedIn, target-role list
Months 3-4   Build core tools   Learn Articulate Storyline or Rise; basic LMS concepts; intro to accessibility and xAPI/SCORM terms; improve visual design   1 short eLearning module
Months 5-6   Create proof of skill   Build 2 portfolio pieces tied to workplace learning; write project case studies; practice SME-to-learning workflow   Portfolio site with 2 projects

Months 7-8   Add job-ready depth   Learn needs analysis, storyboarding, scenario writing, assessment design, basic video editing; understand compliance and onboarding content   3rd portfolio project + storyboard samples
Months 9-10   Enter the market   Apply to Dublin roles; target contract, hybrid, university, EdTech and L&D coordinator paths; network with Irish L&D professionals   30-50 tailored applications

Months 11-12   Convert interviews to offers   Practice portfolio walkthroughs; prepare salary positioning; refine business impact examples and stakeholder communication   Interview-ready portfolio and offer negotiation plan
Skills That Matter Most for Your Move
- Nice-to-have later: Camtasia or Vyond alternatives, basic video editing
- Focus on performance outcomes, not just lesson delivery
- Learn compliance, onboarding, systems training, and soft-skills formats
Skills you already have that transfer well
- Classroom teaching → facilitation and learner engagement
- Assessment design → quiz and performance check creation
- History teaching → strong storytelling and content structuring
- Presentation skills → stakeholder demos and learner-facing content
Option 1:   Learning Designer / Instructional Designer in higher education     Most natural bridge from teaching; values pedagogy strongly   Best fit for your background
Option 2:   L&D Content Specialist in corporate teams     Strong route to €48k+ if you show business-focused portfolio samples   Best salary alignment
Option 3:   eLearning Developer / Junior Instructional Designer     Tool-heavy path using Storyline/Rise and scenario-based modules   Fastest skill-proof route
Option 4:   Training Specialist / Enablement role     Easier first landing if pure ID titles feel competitive; can pivot internally after 6-12 months   Practical stepping stone
-   Articulate 360 trial first   to build initial samples before paying
- 1 strong foundational ID course on adult learning + portfolio thinking
- low-cost practice in accessibility, LMS basics, and case-study writing
-   Optional Canva Pro / video tool / misc.:   €100-€250
-   Buffer for one premium workshop or coaching review:   €300-€700
That pace is enough to produce   3 strong projects in 12 months   if you stay consistent.
Portfolio Projects That Will Make You Employable
Build a 5-8 minute module for new hires on:
- lets you demonstrate concise writing and interaction design
- demonstrates assessment, feedback, and consequence mapping
Design a short training on a common workplace tool:
- very common in corporate ID work
- shows performance support and task-based learning
Take one of your history lessons and convert the structure into a workplace topic:
- proves you can adapt rather than just teach
What each portfolio piece should include
- 3-5 sentence reflection on results and trade-offs
How to Position Your Teaching Experience for €48k+ Roles

Do not present yourself as “a teacher trying something new.” Present yourself as a   learning professional with deep curriculum and learner-engagement experience now specializing in digital workplace learning  .
CV and LinkedIn wording to use
- “Created assessments aligned to measurable learning outcomes”
- “Facilitated learning for diverse audiences with varying support needs”
- “Used data and feedback to improve learner performance”
- “Managed stakeholder communication with students, parents, and school leadership”
Add these target titles to your profile
Your   €48,000 target is achievable  , but it may depend on role type:
-   Most realistic directly at or above target:   corporate L&D content specialist, learning designer, training specialist, some public-sector/higher-ed learning design roles
-   Possible but less certain initially:   junior instructional designer if the role is tool-heavy and you have a thin portfolio
-   Best route if offers come in lower:   take a role in the   €42k-€47k   range only if it gives strong tool exposure and a title/path to move above €48k within 12 months
For your background, the most realistic plan is:
2. target both pure ID roles and adjacent L&D/training roles
3. prioritize employers that value pedagogy, not just corporate experience
